draft.title: Package the app as a multi-architecture Docker image, with a configurable sign-in callback host
draft.context: Running the app needs sbt and a JDK, which makes it hard to install on a home server or Pi. Three things also stop it from working in a container. The Spotify sign-in callback is hard-wired to 127.0.0.1:7070 (`SpotifyClient.serverResource`), so a port published from the container never reaches it. The settings page defaults to 127.0.0.1. And the bundled `application.conf` asks for `beat-source = "audio"`, but a container has no audio device. The app also doesn't say at startup that it is running on Spotify timing.
draft.decision:
Add a config key, `callback.host`, read into a new `CallbackConfig(host: Host)` and validated by its pureconfig reader. It defaults to 127.0.0.1 in reference.conf. The port stays a constant 7070 because the registered redirect URI names it, and the redirect URI itself is unchanged. `SpotifyClient.serverResource` binds to the configured host. `SpotifyClient.resource` gets the config in a second parameter list, so the client's identity (client, creds, store) stays apart from where its callback listens, and it keeps to three parameters.

`Main` logs one line right after loading the config whenever the beat source is Spotify. Logging it before any network work means it shows up even when Spotify or the bridge fails later.

The image is a multi-stage `Dockerfile`:
- Build stage: `eclipse-temurin:21-jdk` plus the arch-neutral sbt launcher tarball. It runs `sbt update` on the build files alone, for layer caching, then `sbt "export root/Runtime/fullClasspath"`. That builds the classes and links the Scala.js page through the existing resourceGenerator, without needing Node. Every classpath entry is copied into `/app/lib` (jars) and `/app/classes`.
- Runtime stage: `eclipse-temurin:21-jre`. Both base images are published for amd64 and arm64, so a plain `docker build` works on either and buildx builds both. No sbt plugins are added.

The image's settings live in `docker/application.conf`, loaded with `-Dconfig.file`. It includes the bundled `classpath("application.conf")`, then sets `callback.host = "0.0.0.0"`, `ui.host = "0.0.0.0"` and `light-show.beat-source = "spotify"`. Last, it does an optional `include file("/config/application.conf")`, which HOCON skips when the file is missing, so a user's read-only mount overrides the light show.

The image sets `ENV SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE=/data/refresh-token` and declares `VOLUME /data`. It runs as a non-root user that owns `/data`, so the token file's 0600/0700 modes hold.
draft.components:
- `domain.config.CallbackConfig` (new): the host plus its `ConfigReader[Host]`. The `Port` constant 7070 lives here too.
- `domain.config.AppConfig`: gains `callback: CallbackConfig = CallbackConfig()`.
- `client.SpotifyClient` (companion): `serverResource(codes, host, port = CallbackConfig.Port)` and `resource(client, creds, store)(callback)`.
- `Main`: logs the Spotify-timing line after the config loads, and passes `config.callback` to `SpotifyClient.resource`.
- `src/main/resources/reference.conf`: adds `callback { host = "127.0.0.1" }` with a comment.
- New files: `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore` (excludes `.env`, `target/`, `project/target`, `.git`, `.bsp`, IDE folders, `node_modules`), `docker/application.conf`.
- Docs: a Docker section in the README; `docs/how-it-works.md` (the sign-in bullet at line 35 and the configuration table); `docs/architecture.md` (the callback box and config types).

Call direction: Main → AppConfig.load (reads CallbackConfig) → SpotifyClient.resource(...)(config.callback) → serverResource(codes, callback.host) → EmberServerBuilder. Nothing calls back into Main.
draft.contracts:
- Config key `callback.host` (string, an IP or host name; default "127.0.0.1" in reference.conf): new and additive. The default keeps today's behaviour.
- `AppConfig`: new field `callback`, with a default. Additive for every existing constructor call and config file.
- `SpotifyClient.serverResource`: gains `host` and `port` (with a default), so it's a source change. Its only caller is `SpotifyClient.resource`.
- `SpotifyClient.resource`: gains a second parameter list, `(callback: CallbackConfig)`. Its only caller is `Main`.
- `SpotifyCredentials`, the redirect URI `http://127.0.0.1:7070/callback`, and the `/callback` endpoint: unchanged.
- Environment variables: none added. The image only presets the existing `SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE=/data/refresh-token`, and `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` still works.
- Settings JSON and the `model` types the settings page shares: unchanged.
- `ui.host` is unchanged as a key; the image's config sets it to 0.0.0.0.
- Image contract (new): it exposes ports 7070 and 7071, uses a volume at `/data`, and reads an optional user config at `/config/application.conf`. It is configured with the README's environment variables.
draft.failureModes:
- Config → app: an invalid `callback.host` (for example "not a host!" or "") is fatal at startup. It surfaces as pureconfig's `CannotConvert` inside the existing `ConfigReaderException`. `Main` already catches that, logs `failures.prettyPrint()` (which names the path `callback.host`) and exits with `ExitCode.Error` before any network call.
- Callback server bind: if the address can't be bound (port 7070 taken, or a host name that isn't a local address), Ember raises a `BindException` from the resource. That is fatal, the same as today.
- Docker build: a failing sbt step fails the build. Nothing about the build is recoverable at runtime.
- Container with no refresh token and no published 7070: sign-in waits forever on the logged authorize URL. That is today's behaviour, and the README covers it.
- No new sealed error type: every new failure is a config-validation failure, and the existing pureconfig failure ADT already carries those.
draft.config:
`callback.host` (default "127.0.0.1", in reference.conf, with a comment). 127.0.0.1 keeps the sign-in callback on this computer. 0.0.0.0 accepts it on any interface; the image uses that so a port published on the host's loopback reaches it.

It's validated at startup by `ConfigReader[Host]`, which uses `Host.fromString` and otherwise gives `CannotConvert(value, "Host", "expected an IP address or host name, such as 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0")`. pureconfig adds the key path, and the app refuses to start.

`docker/application.conf` (image only) sets `callback.host = "0.0.0.0"`, `ui.host = "0.0.0.0"` and `light-show.beat-source = "spotify"`, then includes the optional `/config/application.conf`. The bundled `src/main/resources/application.conf` is unchanged.
draft.observability:
- New INFO line from Main, logged once right after the config loads when `light-show.beat-source` is spotify: "Live beat detection is off because the beat source is Spotify; pulses follow Spotify's playback position and tempo". Its structured field is `beat_source=spotify`. It isn't logged when the beat source is audio.
- An invalid host logs at ERROR through the existing `prettyPrint` line, which names `callback.host` and the rejected value.
- Unchanged: the "Please visit: <authorize URL>" line and the "Settings page at <baseUri>" line, which in the container shows 0.0.0.0:7071.
alternatives: Put the callback host on SpotifyCredentials as `spotify.callback-host`. Why not: SpotifyCredentials derives a circe Codec and holds credentials only. A typed Host there would need its own Codec, and a String would push validation out of the config reader.
Add an environment variable for the host. Why not: the issue rules it out; it has to be a config key.

Use sbt-native-packager or sbt-assembly to package the app. Why not: the issue rules out new sbt plugins. `export Runtime/fullClasspath` plus `java -cp` does the same job with what the build already has.

Mount the user's config over the image's config file. Why not: that would silently drop the image's 0.0.0.0 and spotify settings. An optional include placed after them keeps them and still lets the user's light-show settings win.

package domain.config

import com.comcast.ip4s.{Host, Port, ipv4, port}
import pureconfig.ConfigReader

/**
 * Where the Spotify sign-in callback server listens: `127.0.0.1` keeps it to this computer, `0.0.0.0` accepts it on every
 * interface (as in the Docker image). The port is always 7070, the one the registered redirect URI names.
 */
case class CallbackConfig(host: Host = CallbackConfig.DefaultHost)

object CallbackConfig {

  val DefaultHost: Host = ipv4"127.0.0.1"

  val Port: Port = port"7070"

  given ConfigReader[Host] = ???

  given ConfigReader[CallbackConfig] = ???
}

package domain.config

import cats.effect.kernel.Sync
import domain.spotify.SpotifyCredentials
import domain.config.LightShowConfigReaders.given
import pureconfig.*

case class AppConfig(
  spotify: SpotifyCredentials,
  hue: HueConfig,
  pollingIntervalMs: Int = 2000,
  lightShow: LightShowConfig = LightShowConfig(),
  ui: UiConfig = UiConfig(),
  callback: CallbackConfig = CallbackConfig()
) derives ConfigReader
object AppConfig {
  def load[F[_]: Sync](source: ConfigSource): F[AppConfig] =
    Sync[F].blocking(source.loadOrThrow[AppConfig])
}

slices.title: Configurable callback host, Spotify-timing startup line, and a multi-arch Docker image
slices.delivers: The new `callback.host` key (default 127.0.0.1) bound by the sign-in callback server, the startup line when the beat source is Spotify, the Dockerfile, .dockerignore and docker/application.conf, the README's Docker section, and the updated docs on the callback server. It is one PR: the image depends on the config key, and the key is useful on its own.
acceptanceCriteria: `docker build .` produces an image that starts the app when given only the README's environment variables (SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID, SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET, HUE_BRIDGE_ADDRESS, HUE_USERNAME, HUE_PSK, plus the optional ones).
`docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 .` builds both platforms, and a plain `docker build` builds and runs on an amd64 machine and on an arm64 Raspberry Pi.
With `-p 127.0.0.1:7071:7071`, the settings page opens at http://127.0.0.1:7071 in a browser on the host.
With `-p 127.0.0.1:7070:7070` and no refresh token, opening the logged authorize URL on the host completes sign-in through http://127.0.0.1:7070/callback, and the lights start syncing.
After a browser sign-in, recreating the container with the same named volume at /data starts the app without logging an authorize URL.
In the container, the app plays on Spotify timing without an audio device and logs one line at startup saying live beat detection is off because the beat source is Spotify.
With the default config, the sign-in callback listens on 127.0.0.1:7070 and refuses connections on the machine's non-loopback addresses.
With `callback.host = "0.0.0.0"`, the sign-in callback accepts a GET /callback?code=… on a non-loopback address of the machine and hands the code to the waiting sign-in.
With beat-source spotify, the startup log has exactly one line saying live beat detection is off because the beat source is Spotify; with beat-source audio, it has none.
With `callback.host` set to a value that isn't a host (such as "not a host!" or ""), the app exits with an error code before contacting the bridge, and the error log names `callback.host`.
The README's Docker section shows `docker build .` and `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64`, and says a plain `docker build` works on amd64 or arm64.

The README shows a `docker run` with the environment variables (via --env-file .env), `-p 127.0.0.1:7070:7070`, `-p 127.0.0.1:7071:7071`, and a named volume mounted at /data that keeps the refresh token.
The README shows `ssh -L 7070:localhost:7070 <server>` for signing in on a headless server or Pi, and says setting SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN skips the browser sign-in instead.
The README shows publishing the settings port without 127.0.0.1 to open the page to the local network, and warns that the page has no sign-in, so anyone who can reach it can change the lights.
The README shows mounting your own application.conf read-only at /config/application.conf, and says the settings page's "Copy as config" output goes in that file.

docs/how-it-works.md and docs/architecture.md say the callback server listens on port 7070 at `callback.host`, default 127.0.0.1, and that the Docker image sets it to 0.0.0.0. reference.conf documents the key.
slices.testStrategy:
CallbackConfigSpec, a table over the config loaded with reference.conf: a missing key gives 127.0.0.1; "0.0.0.0" and "localhost" load; invalid values ("not a host!", "", "a b") give a Left whose prettyPrint contains `callback.host`. A property: any generated IPv4 address renders and reads back as the same Host.

SpotifyCallbackServerSpec (CatsEffectSuite): finds a non-loopback IPv4 address of the machine through java.net.NetworkInterface in IO.blocking, and uses `assume` when there is none. It starts `serverResource(codes, host, port"0")`. With the default host, connecting on that address is refused. With 0.0.0.0, GET /callback?code=c on that address returns 200 and `codes` yields "c". It also asserts that `CallbackConfig.Port` is 7070 and the default host is 127.0.0.1.

MainSpec, in the existing style with Tls.capturedLogs and bridgeListener:
- beat-source spotify logs exactly one line with the Spotify-timing message; beat-source audio logs none.
- An invalid `callback.host` gives ExitCode.Error, no bridge connections, and an ERROR line naming `callback.host`.

No TestControl: nothing new is timed.

The Docker criteria are checked by hand in the PR on amd64 and an arm64 Pi (build, run, sign-in, recreate with the volume), because building images in CI is out of scope. The documentation criteria are met by the docs themselves.

findings.headline: Multi-arch buildx build compiles the whole app under slow, crash-prone arm64 emulation
findings.ifIgnored: On an amd64 machine the documented buildx command could take an hour or more, or fail with a JVM crash in the emulated sbt/Scala.js step, so criterion 2 is only shown to work on native hardware.
findings.problem: The build stage is a plain `FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk`. So `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64` runs sbt, the Scala 3 compiler and the Scala.js linker for arm64 under QEMU user emulation. That is very slow, and the JDK's JIT is known to crash under qemu-user. What this stage produces (class files, jars and main.js) doesn't depend on the architecture at all. The PR's manual check (a plain build on each machine) won't catch this, because the cross-build is only ever run emulated.
findings.suggestion: Pin the build stage to the builder's own platform with `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk AS build` and leave the runtime stage per-target. This is still arch-neutral, so a plain `docker build` behaves the same, and buildx compiles once natively. Run the buildx command from an amd64 machine as part of the PR's manual checks.

findings.headline: README's buildx command may build both images and then leave them nowhere usable
findings.ifIgnored: Users who copy the README command get an error from the default builder, or a build with no runnable image, and think the multi-arch support is broken.
findings.problem: The default `docker` buildx driver, without the containerd image store, refuses multi-platform builds. With a `docker-container` builder, a multi-platform build without `--push` or `--output` leaves its results in the build cache only. The design names the command but not the builder setup or where the output goes.
findings.suggestion: In the README, show `docker buildx create --use` (or say the containerd image store is needed), and add `--push -t <registry>/<image>` or an `--output` for the multi-platform command. Say that `--load` only works for a single platform.

findings.headline: Copying the classpath into one flat folder can let jars with the same file name overwrite each other
findings.ifIgnored: If two dependencies ever share a jar file name, one silently replaces the other in /app/lib, and the container fails at runtime with a missing class even though `sbt run` works.
findings.problem: The plan copies every `export root/Runtime/fullClasspath` entry into `/app/lib` by base name, and merges the root and model class directories into one `/app/classes`. Coursier paths keep artifacts apart by group, but base names are not guaranteed unique. Also, `export` prints sbt's `[info]` banner along with the classpath, and the design doesn't say how the build script separates the two (for example `-batch -error` or `tail -n1`).
findings.suggestion: Name how the classpath is captured (`sbt -batch -error 'export root/Runtime/fullClasspath'`). Have the build step fail if two entries share a base name, or keep the order and copy into numbered or group-qualified names, then build the `-cp` from that list.

findings.headline: Leftover build output from subprojects on the host is sent into the image build
findings.ifIgnored: Builds send stale host compile output into the image's build context, which slows builds and risks sbt reusing a host-specific incremental compile state.
findings.problem: In `.dockerignore`, `target/` and `project/target` match only paths at the root of the build context. `ui/target`, `model/.jvm/target`, `model/.js/target` and `project/project/target` are still copied in, including Zinc analysis files that record absolute host paths. `.metals`, `.bloop` and `.idea` are not listed as patterns either.
findings.suggestion: Use `**/target` (plus `.metals`, `.bloop`, `.idea`, `.vscode`) in `.dockerignore`, and keep `.env` and `.env.*` excluded.

findings.headline: Container startup log points users at an unreachable 0.0.0.0 settings address
findings.ifIgnored: Users following the container's own log get a confusing address instead of 127.0.0.1:7071 or the host's address.
findings.problem: The design leaves the 'Settings page at <baseUri>' line unchanged, so in the image it prints `http://0.0.0.0:7071`. That isn't an address a browser on the host should use, and the port the user published can differ from 7071.
findings.suggestion: Have the README say which URL to open (`http://127.0.0.1:<published port>`). Optionally, when the host is 0.0.0.0, log that the page is listening on all interfaces, without changing the line in the default case.

findings.headline: A user's mounted config can quietly undo the image's container settings
findings.ifIgnored: A user who mounts a copy of the repository's application.conf turns audio beat detection back on, or puts the callback back on loopback where the published port can't reach it, and sign-in never completes.
findings.problem: The optional `/config/application.conf` is included after the image's own overrides. The design treats that as a feature, but any `callback.host`, `ui.host` or `light-show.beat-source` in the user's file wins. A full copy of the bundled application.conf (which sets `beat-source = "audio"`) is exactly what many users will mount.
findings.suggestion: In the README, say the mounted file should hold only the light-show lines (the 'Copy as config' output), not a copy of the bundled application.conf. Alternatively, include the user file before the image's three container keys if those should always win.

findings.headline: Network test silently skips on machines with only a loopback address
findings.ifIgnored: On a CI runner or sandbox with no non-loopback IPv4 address, criteria 7 and 8 pass without being checked.
findings.problem: The test picks a non-loopback IPv4 address through NetworkInterface and calls `assume` when there is none. A skipped test counts as green, so the behaviour test for the 0.0.0.0 bind can go unexercised without anyone noticing. The address it picks should also be up, not link-local, and not a down docker bridge.
findings.suggestion: Filter for interfaces that are up and non-virtual, and for site-local or routable IPv4 addresses. Confirm in the PR that the test actually ran rather than being skipped in CI.

draft.title: Package the app as a multi-architecture Docker image, with a configurable sign-in callback host
draft.context: Running the app needs sbt and a JDK. Three more things stop it working in a container. The sign-in callback is hard-wired to 127.0.0.1:7070 (`SpotifyClient.serverResource`). The settings page defaults to 127.0.0.1. And the bundled config asks for `beat-source = "audio"` when a container has no audio device. At startup the app also doesn't say that it is running on Spotify timing.
draft.decision:
Add a new config key, `callback.host`, read into `CallbackConfig(host: Host)` and validated by its pureconfig reader. reference.conf sets its default to 127.0.0.1. The port stays 7070 and the redirect URI doesn't change. `SpotifyClient.resource` takes the config in a second parameter list and passes the host to `serverResource`. Right after loading the config, `Main` logs one line if the beat source is Spotify.

The `Dockerfile` has two stages, and nothing in it is specific to one architecture:
- Build: `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk AS build` with the sbt launcher tarball. The class files, jars and main.js don't depend on the architecture, so buildx compiles once, natively, rather than under QEMU. The stage first runs `sbt update` on the build files alone, so that layer can be cached. Then `sbt -batch -error 'export root/Runtime/fullClasspath' | tail -n1` captures the classpath without sbt's banner, and it also links the Scala.js page through the existing resourceGenerator. Each entry, in order, is copied to `/app/lib/NNN-<basename>` (numbered, so equal base names can't collide). The stage then writes `/app/bin/run`, which runs `java -Dconfig.file=/app/docker.conf -cp <those paths, in order> Main`.
- Runtime: `eclipse-temurin:21-jre`, one per target platform. It runs as a non-root user that owns `/data`, with `ENV SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE=/data/refresh-token` and `VOLUME /data`. No sbt plugins are added.

`docker/application.conf` loads in this order: `include classpath("application.conf")`, then the optional `include file("/config/application.conf")`, then `callback.host = "0.0.0.0"`, `ui.host = "0.0.0.0"` and `light-show.beat-source = "spotify"`. Because the three container keys come last, they win even when a user mounts a full copy of the bundled file.

- `domain.config.CallbackConfig` (new): the host, its `ConfigReader[Host]`, and the `Port` constant 7070.
- `domain.config.AppConfig`: gains `callback: CallbackConfig = CallbackConfig()`.
- `client.SpotifyClient` companion: `serverResource(codes, host, port = CallbackConfig.Port)` and `resource(client, creds, store)(callback)`.
- `Main`: adds `spotifyTiming(config)` and passes `config.callback` on.
- `reference.conf`: adds `callback { host = "127.0.0.1" }`, with a comment.
- New files: `Dockerfile`, `docker/application.conf`, and `.dockerignore` (`**/target`, `.git`, `.bsp`, `.metals`, `.bloop`, `.idea`, `.vscode`, `**/node_modules`, `.env`, `.env.*`).
- Docs: a Docker section in the README; `docs/how-it-works.md` and `docs/architecture.md` change where they describe the callback server.

Calls go in one direction: Main → AppConfig.load → SpotifyClient.resource(…)(config.callback) → serverResource(codes, host) → EmberServerBuilder.
draft.contracts:
- Config key `callback.host` (an IP or host name, default "127.0.0.1"): new and additive. The default keeps today's behaviour.
- `AppConfig.callback`: a new field with a default, so it's additive.
- `SpotifyClient.serverResource` and `SpotifyClient.resource` gain parameters. That's a source change, but their only callers are `resource` and `Main`.
- Unchanged: the redirect URI `http://127.0.0.1:7070/callback`, `/callback`, `SpotifyCredentials`, the settings JSON, the shared `model` types, and the `ui.host` key.
- Environment variables: none are added. The image presets the existing `SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE`, and `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` still works.
- The image itself (new): it exposes 7070 and 7071, keeps the token on the `/data` volume, and reads an optional `/config/application.conf`.
draft.failureModes:
- Config: an invalid `callback.host` is fatal at startup. pureconfig reports it as a `CannotConvert` inside the existing `ConfigReaderException`. `Main` already logs `prettyPrint()`, which names the key, and exits with `ExitCode.Error` before any network call. pureconfig's existing failure ADT carries this, so no new sealed type is needed.
- Callback bind: a port that's taken or an address that isn't local raises a `BindException` from the resource. That's fatal, as it is today.
- Docker build: a failed sbt step or an empty classpath fails the build.
- Container with no token and 7070 not published: sign-in waits on the logged URL, as it does today. The README covers this.
draft.config: `callback.host`, default "127.0.0.1", set in reference.conf with a comment. `ConfigReader[Host]` checks it at startup through `Host.fromString`. Anything else fails with `CannotConvert(value, "Host", "expected an IP address or host name, such as 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0")`, and the app refuses to start. The image sets it to 0.0.0.0 in `docker/application.conf`. The bundled `application.conf` is unchanged.
draft.observability:
- New INFO line from `Main`, logged once right after the config loads when the beat source is spotify. It has the field `beat_source=spotify` and says: "Live beat detection is off because the beat source is Spotify; pulses follow Spotify's playback position and tempo". It isn't logged for audio.
- An invalid host appears in the existing ERROR `prettyPrint` line, with the key and the value.
- The "Settings page at <baseUri>" line is unchanged, so in the image it reads `http://0.0.0.0:7071`. The README therefore tells users to open `http://127.0.0.1:<published port>`.
alternatives: Put the host on `SpotifyCredentials`. Why not: it derives a circe Codec and holds only credentials, so validation would move out of the config reader.
Use sbt-native-packager or sbt-assembly. Why not: the issue rules out new sbt plugins, and `export` plus `java -cp` does the same job.
Include the user's config after the container keys. Why not: a mounted copy of the bundled file would bring back `beat-source = "audio"` and the 127.0.0.1 hosts.

slices.title: Configurable callback host, Spotify-timing startup line, and a multi-arch Docker image
slices.delivers: Delivers everything in one PR, because the image depends on the new config key: the `callback.host` key (default 127.0.0.1), the Spotify-timing startup line, the Dockerfile with `.dockerignore` and `docker/application.conf`, the README's Docker section, and the updated docs on the callback server.
acceptanceCriteria: `docker build .` produces an image that starts the app when given only the README's environment variables.

From an amd64 machine with a `docker-container` builder, `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 .` builds both images and compiles only once, in the build platform's stage. A plain `docker build` builds and runs both on amd64 and on an arm64 Raspberry Pi.
With `-p 127.0.0.1:7071:7071`, the settings page opens at http://127.0.0.1:7071 in a browser on the host.
With `-p 127.0.0.1:7070:7070` and no refresh token, the logged authorize URL completes sign-in through http://127.0.0.1:7070/callback, and the lights start syncing.
After a browser sign-in, recreating the container with the same named volume at /data starts the app without logging an authorize URL.

In the container, with no audio device, the app plays on Spotify timing and logs one startup line saying live beat detection is off because the beat source is Spotify. It does the same when the mounted /config/application.conf sets `beat-source = "audio"`.
With the default config, the sign-in callback listens on 127.0.0.1:7070 and refuses connections on the machine's non-loopback addresses.
With `callback.host = "0.0.0.0"`, the callback accepts GET /callback?code=… on a non-loopback address and hands the code to the waiting sign-in.
With beat-source spotify, the startup log has exactly one line saying live beat detection is off because the beat source is Spotify. With beat-source audio, it has none.
With `callback.host` set to something that isn't a host ("not a host!" or ""), the app exits with an error code before contacting the bridge, and the error log names `callback.host`.

The README shows `docker build .` and says it works on amd64 or arm64. It also shows `docker buildx create --use` (or says the containerd image store is needed) and `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 --push -t <registry>/<image> .`, and says `--load` only works for a single platform.

The README shows a `docker run` with `--env-file .env`, `-p 127.0.0.1:7070:7070`, `-p 127.0.0.1:7071:7071`, and a named volume at /data that keeps the refresh token. It says to open http://127.0.0.1:<published port>, not the 0.0.0.0 address the log prints.
The README shows `ssh -L 7070:localhost:7070 <server>` for signing in on a headless server or Pi, and says setting SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN skips the browser sign-in instead.
The README shows publishing the settings port without 127.0.0.1 to open the page to the local network, and warns that the page has no sign-in, so anyone who can reach it can change the lights.

The README shows mounting your own application.conf read-only at /config/application.conf. It says the file should hold only the light-show lines from the settings page's "Copy as config", not a copy of the bundled application.conf, and that the image's container settings always win.

docs/how-it-works.md and docs/architecture.md say the callback server listens on port 7070 at `callback.host`, which defaults to 127.0.0.1, and that the image sets it to 0.0.0.0. reference.conf documents the key.
slices.testStrategy:
CallbackConfigSpec is a table over configs loaded with reference.conf. A missing key gives 127.0.0.1. "0.0.0.0" and "localhost" load. "not a host!", "" and "a b" give a Left whose prettyPrint names `callback.host`. A property checks that any generated IPv4 address reads back as the same Host.

SpotifyCallbackServerSpec (CatsEffectSuite) finds an IPv4 address in `IO.blocking`. The interface must be up, not loopback, not virtual and not link-local, and the address site-local or routable. If there is none, the test fails when `CI` is set and calls `assume` otherwise, and the PR confirms it ran in CI. The test starts `serverResource(codes, host, port"0")`. With the default host, a connection on that address is refused. With 0.0.0.0, GET /callback?code=c returns 200 and `codes` yields "c". The test also asserts that the port is 7070 and the default host is 127.0.0.1.

MainSpec uses the existing captured-log and fake-bridge harness. With spotify, exactly one Spotify-timing line is logged. With audio, none is. An invalid `callback.host` gives ExitCode.Error, no bridge connections, and an ERROR line naming the key. Nothing new is timed, so there's no TestControl.

The Docker criteria are checked by hand and recorded in the PR: the buildx build from amd64, and a plain build, run, sign-in and recreate on amd64 and on a Pi. Building images in CI is out of scope. The documentation criteria are met by the docs themselves.

findings.headline: Tests never check that the configured host actually reaches the callback server
findings.ifIgnored: The callback.host key could be read and then dropped on the way to the server (Main or resource still binding 127.0.0.1), and every new test would still pass.
findings.problem: Criterion 8 is about the config: when it sets the listen host to 0.0.0.0, the callback accepts non-loopback connections. The planned tests split this into two halves that never meet. CallbackConfigSpec checks that the key parses. SpotifyCallbackServerSpec calls serverResource with a Host it builds itself. Nothing covers config → AppConfig.callback → resource(...)(callback) → serverResource. Main is excluded from coverage, so the coverage gate won't catch it either. resource always binds 7070, which is why the spec avoids calling it, but that also leaves the wiring untested.
findings.suggestion: Make the wiring testable. For example, let resource take the port from CallbackConfig through a package-private or test-only override, or have serverResource take the CallbackConfig. Then add a test that loads `callback.host = "0.0.0.0"` through AppConfig.load, builds the client through resource, and reaches /callback on a non-loopback address.

findings.headline: Plain docker build may fail on a Pi with Debian's older Docker
findings.ifIgnored: On Raspberry Pi OS with the distro docker.io package (20.10, legacy builder), a plain `docker build` may fail on the first FROM line, which breaks criterion 2.
findings.problem: `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` relies on BuildKit filling in BUILDPLATFORM automatically. Docker 23+ uses BuildKit by default. Debian bookworm, and so Raspberry Pi OS, ships docker.io 20.10, which uses the legacy builder by default. With the legacy builder, BUILDPLATFORM is likely to be empty, so the platform string is invalid. The design says a plain build works on a Pi but never states which Docker version or builder that needs.
findings.suggestion: Either state and document the requirement (Docker 23+, or `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1`, with the docker-buildx plugin installed) in the README, and test the plain build on a Pi with the distro package, or make the Dockerfile work without BuildKit's automatic platform args.

findings.headline: Build stage pipes sbt into tail, so a failed sbt run isn't what fails the build
findings.ifIgnored: A broken compile fails the build only by accident, on a later step, with a confusing error. In some cases a bad classpath line could reach the copy step.
findings.section: Decision — Dockerfile build stage; Failure modes — Docker build
findings.problem: `sbt ... 'export root/Runtime/fullClasspath' | tail -n1` takes its exit status from tail. Docker's default RUN shell on the Ubuntu-based temurin image is dash, so `set -o pipefail` may not be available. The design says a failed sbt step fails the build, but nothing makes the pipeline do that.
findings.suggestion: Write sbt's output to a file in its own command (`sbt ... > cp.txt && tail -n1 cp.txt`), or use `SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]`. Then check that every classpath entry exists before copying.

findings.headline: docker stop may kill the app without letting it shut down the light show
findings.ifIgnored: If the script doesn't exec java, `docker stop` waits 10 s and then SIGKILLs the JVM. Resource finalizers, such as stopping the entertainment stream, never run.
findings.problem: The run script "runs java ..." but doesn't say it `exec`s the JVM, or that the ENTRYPOINT uses exec form. If a shell stays as PID 1, it doesn't pass SIGTERM on to java.
findings.suggestion: Say the script ends with `exec java ...` and the ENTRYPOINT uses exec form, or add `--init` / tini.

findings.headline: Default-host refusal test is only meaningful if it reuses the server's bound port
findings.ifIgnored: With port 0, connecting to the LAN address on any other port is refused anyway, so the test proves nothing about the 127.0.0.1 binding.
findings.problem: The spec starts the server on port 0 and asserts that "a connection on that address is refused", but it doesn't say which port it connects to. To show the loopback-only binding, it has to connect to the LAN IP on the server's actual ephemeral port, and should also check that the same port accepts a connection on 127.0.0.1.
findings.suggestion: Name the port explicitly. Connect to `<lan ip>:server.address.port`, assert it's refused, and assert that `127.0.0.1:server.address.port` returns 200 for /callback.

findings.headline: A host name that passes validation can still fail at bind without naming the key
findings.ifIgnored: A typo such as `callback.host = "locahost"` passes the startup check and then fails with an unknown-host error that doesn't mention callback.host.
findings.problem: `Host.fromString` checks only syntax, so any well-formed host name is accepted. Resolution happens later, when Ember binds, and that failure is reported as a generic bind or lookup error rather than through the `prettyPrint` path that names the key.
findings.suggestion: Either accept only IP addresses (plus `localhost`), or note the gap in the Failure modes section so the error isn't presented as covered.

resultJson.title: Add ADR 0004: multi-arch Docker image and configurable callback host
resultJson.body:
Design for LorenzoPrinsloo/spotify-hue-sync#17; doesn't close it.

This adds `docs/adr/0004-…md`, a proposed design for packaging the app as a multi-architecture Docker image. No application code is implemented. The ADR carries typed skeletons with `???` bodies for `CallbackConfig`, `SpotifyClient.serverResource` and `resource`, and `Main.spotifyTiming`.

The ADR proposes:
- A new `callback.host` config key (default `127.0.0.1`), validated at startup, so the sign-in callback can listen on `0.0.0.0` inside a container. The port and redirect URI stay as they are.
- One startup log line from `Main` when the beat source is Spotify.
- A two-stage `Dockerfile` whose build stage is pinned to `$BUILDPLATFORM`. It runs `sbt export root/Runtime/fullClasspath` and starts the app with `java -cp`. No sbt plugins are added.
- A `docker/application.conf` that sets the container's hosts and beat source after an optional mounted `/config/application.conf`, so the container settings always win.

For reviewers: the design went through two critique rounds and was revised once. The second round's findings are not yet addressed in the ADR. They cover testing the config-to-server wiring, whether a plain `docker build` works on older Docker (needed for BuildKit's `$BUILDPLATFORM`), piping `sbt` into `tail`, signal handling in the run script, and host-name validation that only checks syntax.

The diff also includes the `.orca/runs/17a93716431a.progress.json` run record.
